messages:
eli: Heads up — we've got a perf regression on mixtral-8x7b serving after the kernel-picker change last night. p99 token latency up ~12% across long-context chat templates.

maria: repro steps? which routes affected?

eli: repro on canary: long-chat template + system + assistant history (~1.5k tokens). Kernel picker is choosing the byte-fallback kernels more frequently, and KV cache hit-rate drops. sample trace attached via benchmark-bot.

benchmark-bot: profile: avg_token_ms: 3.6 -> 4.0, p99_token_ms: 9.8 -> 11.0, kernel_choice_stats: {fast_kernel: 62%, byte_fallback: 28%, quant_kernel: 10%}, kv_cache_miss_rate: 4% -> 11%

kevin: interesting — saw something similar last month but tied to RoPE scaling mismatch when head_dim != expected for selected kernel. mixtral variant has nonstandard head/kvdims, so kernel-picker heuristics may be misclassifying it as "compatible" with the fast kernel but actually causing misaligned KV memory layout and triggering fallback.

nina: any correlation with tokenization? we had a chat-template change that added extra system messages + a leading space in several prompts.

eli: yes — tokenizer stats show byte-fallback spikes on those routes. When byte-fallback happens we expand tokens and sequence length increases which pushes batch packing into different kernels and busts KV caching.

kevin: quick dump from the trace:```
# kernel trace snippet
step 1: kernel_picker -> fast_kernel (expected)
step 2: tokenizer -> byte_fallback for some messages (rare)
step 3: runtime switches to byte_kernel path -> allocs + kv_cache invalidation
step 4: subsequent requests for same convo choose different kernel -> cache thrash
```

maria: does this only hit mixtral-8x7b? what about qwen/x-7b or llama-2 7b?

eli: mixtral shows the worst delta. qwen-7b shows mild p95 increase (~3%), llama-2 seems stable. hypothesis: mixtral's head_dim / kv layout + our updated kernel heuristics + tokenizer-induced token variance combine to make the kernel picker flip-flop.

kevin: actionable ideas: 1) short-term: add a flag to force kernel selection based on model id (force_fast_kernel_for: [llama-2], avoid_fast_for: [mixtral-8x7b]) so we stop the thrash; 2) medium: tighten kernel-picker to prefer kernel stability over marginal perf for first N requests in a conv; 3) long: add per-model kernel profiles recorded at model onboarding time and use them to seed picker.

nina: +1 on forcing per-model decisions. also we should normalize chat templates at the frontend to avoid tokenization edge-cases (strip leading spaces, collapse repeated system messages) — that will reduce byte-fallback triggers.

eli: quick mitigation plan I'm going to try: revert the picker tweak on canary and add a per-model override for mixtral-8x7b. deploying now. /deploy canary kernel-picker-revert --image=runtime:v2026-03-18-canary

benchmark-bot: canary deployed to 10% hosts. running 30m perf job. link: https://perf.internal/redwood/runs/1905006789-canary

maria: after canary results we should add a short test in model-onboard CI to validate head_dim vs kernel assumptions. also add tokenizer regression test that runs a few chat-template permutations and ensures no unexpected byte-fallback increase.

kevin: one more note — RoPE scaling: when we scale RoPE for long context we must ensure kernel selection uses the scaled-compat kernels. otherwise cos/sin tables mismatch cause fallback. I'll add a unit test for that.

eli: thanks. I'll monitor canary and post results. if canary looks good we'll push full revert and schedule the picker-hardening work for next sprint.

nina: thanks team. can we also add a lightweight alert in console when kv_cache_miss_rate > 5% for a route? this would have flagged earlier.

maria: added ticket: PROD-1248 add kv miss alert + model-kernel overrides + tokenizer-normalization checklist.

eli: closing loop — canary p99 improved back down to ~9.9 after revert, kv_miss back to 3%. will create PR for per-model overrides and the tokenizer normalization RFC.

kevin: pls include a short profiling snippet in the PR (how to reproduce + flame graph) and mark models that need special handling (mixtral variants).

benchmark-bot: perf run complete: baseline vs canary diff: p99 -1.1ms, kv_miss -8pp, byte_fallback_rate -6pp. artifacts uploaded.

nina: awesome. follow-up tasks assigned. :thumbsup:
